panels.description: Total log entries matching $filter in the selected time range. Use to sanity-check ingestion volume, baseline changes after deploys, or quickly count specific events by refining the filter (e.g., level:=error).
panels.title: Total logs

panels.description: Time since the newest matching log. Use to detect pipeline delay or backpressure; alert if it exceeds your acceptable threshold.

targets.expr: $filter | first 1 by (_time desc) | math (now() - _time) default 0 as lag_ns | max(lag_ns) as lag_ns

panels.title: Last Log Age

panels.description: Records-per-second over time for the current filter. Use to spot bursts/drops, correlate with incidents, and validate throttling or autoscaling effects.
panels.title: Log ingestion rate

panels.description:
Fields are ranked by storage consumption (including `bytes/row`). Use this to find storage-heavy or poorly compressing fields (high `bytes/row` but relatively few `rows`) and consider:

- dropping unused fields, 
- splitting dense text into structured keys.

```
{
  "level": "info",
  "user_id": "alice",
  "product.id": "123",
  "product.name": "Super Widget",
  "product.category": "widgets",
  "product.attributes.color": "red",
  "product.attributes.size": "large",
  "product.price": "2999",
  "_msg": "paid"
}
```

targets.expr:
$filter
  | block_stats
  | stats by (field)
      sum(values_bytes) as values_bytes,
      sum(bloom_bytes) as bloom_bytes,
      sum(rows) as rows
  | math
      (values_bytes+bloom_bytes) as total_bytes,
      round(total_bytes / rows, 0.01) as bytes_per_row
  | sort by (total_bytes desc) limit $limit
  | total_stats min(total_bytes) as min_total_bytes, max(total_bytes) as max_total_bytes

panels.title: Top $limit heaviest fields

panels.description:
Number of field names that appear in ≤ dangling_threshold ($dangling_threshold) logs within the selected time range. 

A high count often points to typos, inconsistent naming, or one-off fields that bloat schema and storage. Use this to target cleanup: standardize key names, fix instrumentation, or drop ephemeral fields. Increase the threshold to widen the search.
panels.title: Dangling field names (threshold: $dangling_threshold)

panels.description: This panel is a useful tool for schema discovery.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | field_names
  | sort by (hits desc) limit $limit
  | total_stats max(hits) as max_count, min(hits) as min_count
  | math min_count%max_count as min_count

panels.title: Top $limit field names (desc)

panels.description: Least frequently present field names. Use this to find stale, rare, or dynamic keys that can be removed. Dangling field names can be harmful because they are treated as columns in storage. Having many stable field names is fine, but having too many field names over time is not.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | field_names
  | sort by (hits asc) limit $limit
  | total_stats max(hits) as max_count, min(hits) as min_count

panels.title: Top $limit field names (asc)

panels.description:
This panel shows the most frequently seen logs, it is extremely valuable for:
- Operations teams: Spotting noisy logs
- Developers: Understanding application behavior
- Cost optimization: Identifying high-volume logs to reduce
- Debugging: Finding common error patterns

Click on the log to drill down and see the specific logs that belong to that pattern.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | collapse_nums prettify
  | stats by (_msg) count() as hits
  | sort by (hits desc) limit $limit
  | total_stats max(hits) as max_count, min(hits) as min_count
  | rename _msg msg

panels.title: Top $limit _msg patterns (desc)

panels.description:
This panel tells you which specific field=value pairs dominate your filtered logs right now (excluding stream metadata), so you can act fast. Some practical use cases:

Incident triage (last 10–30m, errors)
- See which endpoint, status, pod, namespace, error_code, or client_ip shows up most.

Noisy source hunt (info logs)
- Identify the chattiest user_agents, clients, hosts, or paths driving volume.

Data quality/enrichment check
- Spot bad values like namespace=unknown or service=missing bubbling into the top list.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | facets
  | filter -field_name:in(_stream_id,_stream)
  | sort by (hits) desc limit $limit
  | total_stats max(hits) as max_count, min(hits) as min_count

panels.title: Top $limit fields (key-value pair)

panels.description: Tracks how many distinct log streams exist in the logs that match your filter. The result tells you the size/complexity of the selected dataset (how many unique stream signatures are active), which is practical for tracking stream cardinality, scope of activity, and changes over time.
panels.title: Total streams

panels.description:
This panel gives you a time series of "how many distinct log streams are active" per interval, so you can see the footprint and churn of your logs over time.

Watch for spikes that signal cardinality explosions after a config change, sudden drops that indicate ingestion gaps or outages, and steady growth that drives storage and index pressure.
panels.title: Active streams (step: $__interval) (cardinality)

panels.description: Busiest streams by log count. Use to identify top talkers for tuning (log level, sampling) and to focus triage/drilldowns on high-impact producers.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | stats by (_stream) count() as hits
  | first $limit (hits desc)
  | copy _stream as stream
  | fields stream, hits
  | total_stats max(hits) as max_count, min(hits) as min_count

panels.title: Top $limit streams (asc)

panels.description:
It measures how many low-activity streams you have within the window. 

A rising population of tiny streams usually means your stream value includes high‑cardinality fields (IDs, timestamps, random tokens) or an agent is mislabeling logs. That fragments data into many small streams, increases index/metadata overhead, and slows queries even if each stream is small.

targets.expr: $filter | stats (_stream) count() as hits | hits:<=$dangling_threshold | count()

panels.title: Total dangling streams (dangling_threshold: $dangling_threshold)

panels.description: Streams with the smallest log counts in the current window. Surface quiet or stale streams that may need attention.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | stats by (_stream) count() as hits
  | first $limit (hits asc)
  | copy _stream as stream
  | fields stream, hits
  | total_stats max(hits) as max_count, min(hits) as min_count

panels.title: Top $limit (dangling) streams (asc)

panels.description: Per-group log throughput (RPS) for a selectable field. Use to compare namespaces/pods/services, pinpoint hot spots, and confirm whether traffic shifts match expectations.

targets.expr:
$filter
  | stats by ($group) rate() as value
  | sort by (value desc) limit $limit
  | total_stats max(value) as max_count, min(value) as min_count
  | rename _stream as __stream
  | rename value "~value"

panels.title: Records/s by ($group)

panels.description:
Ranks your chosen groups by total log payload, so you can see which dimensions produce the most bytes. 

Use it to find "top talkers" by volume (cost and storage drivers), spot overly verbose components, and decide where to reduce noise or sample. Set $group to the dimension you care about (for example, service, namespace, pod, path)

targets.expr:
$filter
  | stats by ($group) sum_len() as value
  | sort by (value desc) limit 10
  | total_stats max(value) as max_count, min(value) as min_count
  | rename _stream as __stream
  | rename value "~value"

panels.title: Bytes (length) by ($group)

panels.description: Recent 500 logs matching $filter. Use for quick spot checks, validating patterns from the tables above, and sampling before writing more specific filters.
panels.title: Logs (limit 500)
Drilldown (used by the panels above, not used directly)

panels.description: It’s a drilldown to inspect real log lines that match a chosen message template.
panels.title: Logs by pattern (limit 500)

list.description:
Custom LogsQL filter attached to every query.
Type any word or phrase you want to look for. Set to "*" to not filter.
See https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/logsql/#word-filter
list.name: filter
